content.p: As a general rule, Federal Council sessions shall be held once a week.
Business of major importance or political significance shall be discussed and decided individually. Business of far-reaching significance may be dealt with in the context of closed-door meetings.

The remaining business may, if uncontested, be passed as a whole without individual discussion or may be dealt with by written resolution. Presidential decisions pursuant to Article 26 paragraph 4 GAOA remain reserved.
Amended by No I of the O of 21 Aug. 2002, in force since 1 Oct. 2002 (AS 2002 2827).

If circumstances require it and there is no time to hold a meeting, the Federal Council may also discuss individual items of business as mentioned in paragraph 2 in writing or by other means. These resolutions are equivalent to those taken at meetings. Presidential decisions pursuant to Article 26 paragraphs 1-3 GAOA remain reserved.
Amended by No I of the O of 21 Aug. 2002, in force since 1 Oct. 2002 (AS 2002 2827).
The resolutions shall be recorded in writing for each item of business.

article.heading: Business planning
article.subheading: (Art. 25 para. 2 let. a, 32 let. b and 33 GAOA)

content.p: Business planning shall ensure that business can be dealt with in the Federal Council in accordance with its importance and urgency.

The President of the Confederation, in consultation with the Federal Chancellery and the departments, shall determine the most important items of business and thematic priorities for a quarter or semester.

article.heading: Proposals, special discussions and briefing notes

content.p: As a general rule, the Federal Council shall take its decisions on the basis of written proposals and after the joint reporting procedure has been completed (Art. 5).
The members of the Federal Council and, for the business of the Federal Chancellery, the Federal Chancellor have the right to submit proposals.

Where federal law designates other authorities or bodies that may submit business or proposals to the Federal Council, this shall be done via the Federal Chancellery or the department that has the closest technical connection with the business in question.

The Federal Council shall hold special discussions in particular on matters of far-reaching importance. If necessary, it shall take interim decisions, determine the main features of a solution and issue instructions to the competent department or the Federal Chancellery on how to deal with the matter.
The departments or the Federal Chancellery may at any time, without formal request, send the Federal Council briefing notes on important processes and activities in their area of responsibility.

When preparing proposals, the lead office shall invite jointly interested administrative units to comment, setting appropriate deadlines. In justified exceptional cases, the office consultation procedure may be waived or may be limited to a narrow group of addressees.

In the case of confidential and secret Federal Council business, the administrative units responsible for advance legal examination shall be consulted on important and contentious legal issues before the Federal Council meeting if possible.
Inserted by Annex No 1 of the Organisation Ordinance of 29 Nov. 2013 for the Federal Council, in force since 1 Jan. 2014 (AS 2013 4561).
Differences shall be resolved as far as possible through the office consultation procedure; the lead department shall report on this to the Federal Council.
The administrative units that have a technical connection to the business or that are responsible for the assessment of financial, legal or formal aspects are considered to be co-interested.

The joint-reporting procedure serves to prepare for the decision-making process at Federal Council level. The aim of the procedure is to enable the Federal Council to concentrate on fundamental aspects in its deliberations.

The joint reporting procedure begins with the signing of the proposal by the lead department.
Inserted by Annex 2 No 1 of the Public Order of 24 May 2006, in force since 1 July 2006 (AS 2006 2331).

The lead department shall submit the signed proposal to the Federal Chancellery in good time for conducting the joint-reporting procedure.

chapter.heading: Requests for Information from Council Members and Parliamentary Committees

content.p:
The competent department shall decide on requests from Council members and from parliamentary committees for information in accordance with Articles 7 or 150 of the Parliament Act of 13 December 2002
SR 171.10 (ParlA). If there is disagreement between the applicant and the competent department on the scope of the rights to information, the Federal Council shall decide.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council shall decide in each case:

item.p: in the case of information that directly serves its decision-making, at the request of the Federal Chancellery;
in the case of information relating to state security and the intelligence services at the request of the competent department.

content.p: Requests to inspect Federal Council decisions are processed and answered by the Federal Chancellery in consultation with the competent department.

chapter.heading: Consultation of the Parliamentary Committees responsible for Foreign Policy

blockList.listIntroduction:
The committees responsible for foreign policy shall be consulted on important plans within the meaning of Article 152 paragraphs 3 and 4 ParlA
SR 171.10 in particular when:

item.p: as a result of the implementation of recommendations or decisions of international organisations or multilateral bodies, the enactment or a substantial amendment of a federal act is required; or

failure to implement such recommendations or decisions would entail the risk of serious economic disadvantages, sanctions, isolation of Switzerland due to the dissenting Swiss position or political reputational damage, or if other serious disadvantages for Switzerland are to be expected.

content.p: Consultation in accordance with paragraph 1 shall take place on the basis of a draft mandate from the Federal Council. In the case of urgent consultations in accordance with Article 152 paragraph 4 ParlA, consultation may take place on provisional positions that Switzerland intends to adopt in negotiations.

item.p: confidential or secret international treaties or decisions under international law, as well as their amendment or repeal.

section.heading: Structure of the Federal Administration

content.p: The Federal Administration is divided into the central and the decentralised administration.

Public or private entities that have been created by statute and predominantly provide services of a monopolistic nature or perform economic or security supervisory tasks fall within the scope of the decentralised federal administration.

External providers of administrative tasks within the meaning of Article 2 paragraph 4 GAOA that predominantly provide services on the market are not part of the Federal Administration’s. This also applies to private law entities which the Confederation supports with financial assistance or contributions under Article 3 of the Subsidies Act of 5 October 1990
SR 616.1 or in which it holds a minority interest.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Decentralised Federal Administration comprises the following four categories of administrative units:

item.p: the extra-parliamentary commissions pursuant to Article 57a GAOA;

the legally independent public corporations and foundations as well as institutions established by statute, unless they predominantly provide services on the market;
companies limited by shares which the Confederation controls in terms of capital and voting rights, unless they predominantly provide services on the market.

content.p: The administrative units in accordance with paragraph 1 letters a and b are not bound by directives in the performance of their duties unless the law provides otherwise.

section.heading: Extra-Parliamentary Commissions

content.p: Extra-parliamentary commissions are either administrative or executive commissions, depending on their function.
Administrative commissions have advisory and preparatory functions.
Executive commissions have decision-making powers.
Any person who fulfils the requirements for employment in the Federal Administration may be elected as a member of an extra-parliamentary commission.

There is no age restriction for election.
Inserted by No I of the O of 27 June 2012, in force since 1 Aug. 2012 (AS 2012 3819).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I 1 of the O of 9 Dec. 2022 on the Adaptation of Ordinances as a Result of the 2022 Review of the Extra-Parliamentary Commissions, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 842).

content.p: At least of the members of an extra-parliamentary commission must be women, and at least 40 per cent must be men. In the longer term, equal representation of both genders should be aimed for.
If the proportion of women or men is less than 40 per cent, the Federal Chancellery shall request the department concerned to provide written justification.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by Annex No II 2 of the Language Ordinance of 4 June 2010, in force since 1 July 2010 (AS 2010 2653).

content.p: As far as possible, German, French and Italian speakers must be represented in the extra-parliamentary commissions. At least one Romansh-speaking person should be sought.
If German, French and Italian are not represented by at least one person, the Federal Chancellery shall request the department concerned to provide written justification.

article.heading: Exceeding the legal maximum number of members

content.p: Exceeding the statutory maximum number of members of extra-parliamentary commissions is only permitted in exceptional cases and must be justified.

blockList.listIntroduction: An excess number of members is justified in particular if:

item.p: two or more commissions are merged;
a balanced composition is only possible with a higher number of members;
because of the importance of the police field for which the commission is responsible, a broader inclusion of different points of view is required.

content.p: Extra-parliamentary commissions shall be established by order of the Federal Council.

article.heading: Waiting period for members of commissions entrusted with supervisory and regulatory tasks

content.p: The Federal Council may set a waiting period in its decision electing members of commissions entrusted with supervisory and regulatory tasks if it is to be expected that the immediate appointment of a member after leaving the commission to a position with employers or clients in the area supervised or regulated will lead to a conflict of interest.

blockList.listIntroduction: A conflict of interest exists in particular if:

item.p: the credibility and reputation of the commission or the Confederation may be adversely affected by the appointment;

a commission member has influence over individual decisions or access to information in such a way that he or she would no longer appear to be impartial if he or she worked for an employer or client in the regulated or supervised sector.

content.p: The duration of the waiting period shall be a minimum of six and a maximum of twelve months.

Compensation may be stipulated for the waiting period. It shall correspond to in the financial loss to be expected in the individual case but shall not exceed the remuneration previously received, whereby all income, expenses and pension benefits received in this period shall be taken into account.
Any person who receives compensation during a waiting period allowance is obliged to report the income, expenses and pension benefits received during the waiting period to the competent department.
Any waiting period compensation received without justification must be refunded.

authorialNote.p: See also para. 2 of the transitional provision to the amendment of 26 Nov. 2008 at the end of this text.

content.p: Commission members may use information that is not publicly known that they obtain in the course of their commission activities only for their commission activities.
In particular, they may not use information under paragraph 1 to gain an advantage for themselves or others.

The term of office of members of extra-parliamentary commissions shall be four years. It is based on the legislature period of the National Council. It begins on 1 January und ends on 31 December.
Amended by No I of the O of 27 June 2012, in force since 1 Aug. 2012 (AS 2012 3819).
The mandate of members elected during the term of office shall end on its expiry.
The Federal Council shall hold general elections for each new term of office of the extra-parliamentary commissions.
The Federal Chancellery shall coordinate the general elections. It shall issue the corresponding directives for this purpose and shall make them known to the Federal Assembly control committees.
After the general elections, the Federal Chancellery shall submit a report to the Federal Council on the composition of the extra-parliamentary commissions for the attention of the Federal Assembly.
The term of office of members of extra-parliamentary commissions shall be limited to a total of twelve years; it shall end on the expiry of the corresponding calendar year.
In justified individual cases, the Federal Council may extend the term of office to a maximum of 16 years.
The term limit does not apply to federal employees whose membership is necessary for the performance of their duties or is made mandatory by another enactment.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 19 Dec. 2012, in force since 1 Feb. 2013 (AS 2013 205).

content.p: Each extra-parliamentary commission shall have a secretariat that shall be run by an office in the Central Federal Administration.
The head and the other employees of the Secretariat are subject to the federal law on personnel that applies in the Central Federal Administration.
Derogating provisions of specific legislation or provisions in the election order shall remain reserved.

article.heading: Provision of information to the public

content.p: Commissions that may in terms of their election order communicate without consulting the competent authority shall exercise due restraint when providing the public with information on political issues.

section.heading: Remuneration of Members of Extra-Parliamentary Commissions

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 19 Dec. 2012, in force since 1 Feb. 2013 (AS 2013 205).

content.p: Any person who has been elected as a member or as a substitute member of an extra-parliamentary commission and who serves on that commission shall be entitled to remuneration in terms of this Section.

article.heading: Social policy and market policy commissions

blockList.listIntroduction: The extra-parliamentary administrative and executive commissions are subdivided in terms of the remuneration of their members into:

item.p: social policy commissions that support the Federal Assembly, the Federal Council and the Federal Administration and deal primarily with social policy issues;
market policy commissions that supervise or significantly support the functioning of a market.

article.heading: Remuneration categories of social policy commissions

blockList.listIntroduction: The social policy commissions shall be allocated to the following remuneration categories with regard to the remuneration of their members in accordance with the requirements for the members and with the tasks of the commission:

item.p: Category G3, if the commission’s activities require a high level of specific expertise from its members, namely if the members must be technical authorities in the commission’s field and possess knowledge that cannot be acquired at short notice;
Category G2, if the commission’s activities require a high level of general expertise from its members and the commission has sovereign decision-making powers;
Category G1, if the commission’s activities require a high level of general expertise from its members and the commission has advisory tasks.

content.p:
The allocation of the social policy commissions to the compensation categories is regulated in Annex 2 number 1.
Amended by No I of the O of 30 June 2010, in force since 1 Aug. 2010 (AS 2010 3175).

article.heading: Remuneration of members of social policy Commissions

content.p: The members and substitute members of social policy commissions are entitled to a daily allowance for their commission activities.

The rates listed in Annex 2 Number 1 apply. These apply to the Vice-President and to the other members.
Amended by No I of the O of 30 June 2010, in force since 1 Aug. 2010 (AS 2010 3175).
The President shall receive a daily allowance of 25 per cent more. In justified exceptional cases, the competent authority may pay the President a maximum of twice the daily allowance.

blockList.listIntroduction: If the specific legislation or the establishment order requires a member of a commission to be independent of the industry whose activities fall within the commission’s remit, and if this restricts the member in the exercise of his or her professional activities, the competent authority may:

item.p: increase his or her daily allowance by a maximum of 50 per cent; in the case of the President, a daily allowance that has been increased in accordance with paragraph 3 shall be taken into account; and

pay the member a lump sum of no more than CHF 30,000 per year in addition to his or her daily allowance; the lump sums paid shall be shown and justified in the report on the general elections in accordance with Article 8h paragraph 3.
Inserted by No I of the O of 27 June 2012 (AS 2012 3819). Amended by No I of the O of 9 Dec. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 4813).

content.p:
If a member is exceptionally required to work outside of meetings and inspections in studying files and reports or preparing papers, the competent authority may pay him or her a maximum of 16 additional daily allowances per year. If an assignment stipulated in the specific legislation requires more time or effort, the competent authority may authorise the payment of more than 16 additional daily allowances in individual cases. If more than the 16 additional daily allowances are paid, this shall be reported and justified in the report on the general elections pursuant to Article 8h paragraph 3.
Amended by No I of the O of 19 Dec. 2012, in force since 1 Feb. 2013 (AS 2013 7427).

If a member of the Commission has to leave his or her place of residence on the day before the meeting or is only able to return there on the day after the meeting, the competent authority shall pay him or her half a daily allowance for the day of travel.
It is not permitted to claim several daily allowances for one and the same day, even if several different or separately calculable activities have been carried out.
The rates are not adjusted to take account of inflation.

article.heading: Remuneration categories for market policy commissions

blockList.listIntroduction: The market policy commissions shall be allocated to the following compensation categories with regard to the compensation of their members depending on the impact of the results of their work:

item.p: Category M3, if the results of the commission’s work have an impact on the national economy as a whole;
Category M2/A, if the results of the commission’s work have an influence on an entire industry;
Category M2/B, if the results of the commission’s work have an influence on an entire industry, but the commission only supports the functioning of a market and does not supervise it;
Category M1, if the results of the commission’s work have an influence on an industrial sector or if the commission performs tasks involving arbitration.

content.p:
The allocation of the market policy commissions to the remuneration categories is regulated in Annex 2 paragraph 2.
Amended by No I of the O of 30 June 2010, in force since 1 Aug. 2010 (AS 2010 3175).

article.heading: Remuneration of members of market policy commissions

content.p: The members of market policy commissions are entitled to lump-sum compensation for their commission activities.

The rates listed in Annex 2 number 2 apply.
Amended by No I 1 of the O of 9 Dec. 2022 on the Adaptation of Ordinances as a Result of the 2022 Review of the Extra-Parliamentary Commissions, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2022 842).
These rates include all costs, with the exception of the reimbursement of expenses.

The rates apply to a full-time workload; the basis for calculation is 220 working days per year. In the case of part-time positions, the degree of employment shall be determined in the election resolution, if it is not specified in the regulations on the organisation of the commission concerned.
Amended by No I of the O of 27 June 2012, in force since 1 Aug. 2012 (AS 2012 3819).
The rates are not adjusted to take account of inflation.
The reimbursement of expenses for members and substitute members of extra-parliamentary commissions shall be governed by the corresponding provisions for federal staff.

Members who are required to take special organisational measures to look after children or relatives in need of care in order to work for the commission may apply to the competent authority for reimbursement of their expenses.
Inserted by No I of the O of 19 Dec. 2012, in force since 1 Feb. 2013 (AS 2013 205).
Members and substitute members of extra-parliamentary commissions who are in an employment relationship with the Central or Decentralised Federal Administration are not entitled to remuneration.
The competent authority may grant exceptions if membership of the commission is not connected with employment with the Central or Decentralised Federal Administration.
Remuneration for business trips, meals and overnight stays shall be in accordance with the provisions applicable to such members.

Members of extra-parliamentary commissions may only be remunerated at the rates applicable to their commission. Additional remuneration for activities related to the mandate of the Commission shall be excluded.

chapter.heading: Direction of Government and Administrative Activities

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Administration shall act within the bounds of federal law and of the aims and priorities set by the Federal Council. It shall observe the following principles in particular:

item.p: It recognises any new need for action at an early stage and derives aims, strategies and measures from this.
It arranges its activities according to importance and urgency.
It provides its services in a citizen-oriented, sustainable, effective and economical manner.

blockList.listIntroduction: Managers at all levels shall act in accordance with the following principles:

item.p: They lead by agreeing on objectives and impacts.
They shall periodically assess the performance of their administrative units and their employees.
They shall adapt processes and organisation to new needs in a timely manner.
They shall use their room for manoeuvre and decision-making powers and also grant these to their employees.
They shall promote a culture of willingness to learn and change.
They shall ensure a result-oriented and interdisciplinary way of working.

content.p: In all other respects, the personnel legislation and the Federal Council’s personnel policy guidelines apply in particular.

article.heading: Assignment of responsibilities at the appropriate level in der Central Federal Administration

content.p: The significance of an item of business shall be decisive for the allocation of responsibility for taking a decision in accordance with Article 47 paragraph 1 GAOA.

As a rule, responsibility shall be allocated to the unit where the required political and technical competence is concentrated. Assignment to units below office level shall only be made in justified exceptional cases.
In individual cases, an item of business shall be submitted to the next higher unit for a decision or for the issuing of a directive if its particular importance or complexity so requires.
Administrative units are obliged to cooperate. They support and inform each other.
They shall coordinate their activities and align them with the overall policy of the Federal Council.
They shall provide other administrative units with the information required for the fulfilment of their statutory duties.

article.heading: Participation of administrative units with an interest

content.p:
Administrative units shall ensure the participation of all units with an interest in the preparation of their decisions.
Amended by Art. 53 para. 2 of the Publications Ordinance of 7 Oct. 2015, in force since 1 Jan. 2016 (AS 2015 3989).

For this purpose, they shall invite the units with an interest to submit a written opinion, unless another enactment provides for a different form of participation.
Amended by Art. 53 para. 2 of the Publications Ordinance of 7 Oct. 2015, in force since 1 Jan. 2016 (AS 2015 3989).

The provisions on Federal Council business (Art. 4) apply mutatis mutandis to participation in the preparation of legislative texts.
Inserted by Art. 53 para. 2 of the Publications Ordinance of 7 Oct. 2015, in force since 1 Jan. 2016 (AS 2015 3989).
If consent is required, differences shall be settled by the units involved themselves. Exceptionally, they may demand a settlement of differences at the next higher level.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No II of the O of 11 March 2016, in force since 1 April 2016 (AS 2016 929).

article.heading: Cooperation with the cantons and other executive agencies

content.p: If a federal project affects essential cantonal or communal interests, the department concerned or the Federal Chancellery shall involve the cantonal bodies concerned and, if appropriate, the national umbrella organisations for communes, towns and mountain regions in an appropriate manner.

blockList.listIntroduction: Essential interests in accordance with paragraph 1 are affected in particular if:

item.p: the project is to be implemented in whole or in part by cantonal or communal bodies and implementation requires considerable human or financial resources on their part;
cantonal or communal bodies must be reorganised; or
cantonal or communal bodies must make significant changes to the law.

content.p: The Conference of Secretaries General is the supreme coordinating body. It contributes to ensuring forward-looking, effective and coherent administrative action. It shall involve other persons or bodies.
It participates in the planning, preparation and execution of Federal Council business and in the settlement of differences.

The Federal Council shall issue regulations on how the Conference is organised and on its working methods.
Inserted by Annex No 5 of the O of 25 Nov. 2020 on Digital Transformation and Information Technology, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 5871).

article.heading: Planning
article.subheading: (Art. 6 para. 1, 25 para. 2 let. a, 32 let. a, 36 para. 1, 51, 52 GAOA)

content.p: The Federal Council shall decide on the priorities, aims and means required for planning.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council’s plans comprise:

item.p: specific plans for individual federal policy fields or parts thereof;
further plans as required.

content.p: The sectoral and financial plans shall be coordinated as far as possible in terms of timing and content. The individual areas of responsibility are grouped into policy fields.

The Federal Chancellery shall prepare the sectoral plans in accordance with paragraph 2 letter a. The Federal Finance Administration (FFA)
Name in accordance with No I of the O of 11 March 2022, in force since 1 July 2022 (AS 2022 179). This amendment has been made in the provisions specified in the AS. shall prepare the budget and financial plan. In doing so, they work with the departments.
The plans of the Federal Council and the departments are binding for their subordinate administrative units.
Government policy guidelines provide a comprehensive policy orientation framework for government activity in a legislature period.
They assess the results of the previous legislature period.
They define the aims, impacts and priority measures and designate the areas in which state services must be reviewed or can be reduced.

article.heading: Annual objectives of the Federal Council

content.p: The annual objectives of the Federal Council shall set out the main features of the government’s activities for the coming year, specify aims and measures and designate the business to be approved for submission to the Federal Assembly.

The annual objectives form a basis for the Federal Council’s business planning in accordance with Article 2, for controlling in accordance with Article 21, for supervision in accordance with Section 5 and for annual business reporting in accordance with Article 45 of the Parliamentary Procedure Act of 23 March 1962
See now the Parliament Act of 13 Dec. 2002 (SR 171.10). (ParlPA).

article.heading: Annual objectives of the departments and the Federal Chancellery

content.p: The departments and the Federal Chancellery shall coordinate their annual objectives with the Federal Council’s plans and submit them to the Federal Council for approval.

They shall report on their activities as part of the Federal Council’s annual business report in accordance with Article 45 ParlPA
See now the Parliament Act of 13 Dec. 2002 (SR 171.10). .
Controlling is a management instrument for the process-related monitoring of the achievement of objectives at all levels.
The Federal Council shall be supported in its controlling by the Federal Chancellery and the Federal Department of Finance. They shall work with the departments.
The departments are responsible for controlling in their area. They shall coordinate their controlling with the Federal Council’s controlling.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Art. 20 No 3 of the GEVER Ordinance of 3 April 2019, in force since 1 April 2020 (AS 2019 1311).

content.p: The administrative units shall maintain records of their own business activities using a records management system.

For this purpose, they shall use electronic records and process management systems in accordance with the GEVER Ordinance of 3 April 2019
SR 172.010.441 , unless legislation provides for a different type of records and process management.

article.heading:
Responsibilities
Inserted by No I of the O of 19 June 2024, in force since 1 Aug. 2024 (AS 2024 313).

content.p: The Federal Chancellery, in cooperation with the departments, shall be responsible for informing the Federal Assembly, the cantons and the public about the Federal Council’s decisions, intentions and measures. It shall attend to the required planning and draw up principles for the Federal Council’s communication policy.

The departments and the Federal Chancellery shall be responsible for internal and external information and communication on their business. They shall place these in the overall context of the Federal Council’s communication policy. They shall regulate the information tasks of the units subordinate to them.

The Federal Chancellery, in cooperation with the Conference of Information Services, shall be responsible for the coordination of information and communication and may issue directives for this purpose.

If necessary, the Federal Council may centralise information and communication with the President of the Confederation, the Federal Chancellery, a department or another designated office. The designated body shall be given appropriate powers of to issue directives.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 19 June 2024, in force since 1 Aug. 2024 (AS 2024 313).

blockList.listIntroduction: Administrative units may operate their own presences (profiles) on social media in order to provide information insofar as:

item.p: the content of these profiles is accessible to all persons over the age of majority who are resident in Switzerland;
they can make their profiles and content inaccessible at any time.

content.p: Information provided on social media must also be available via channels that the administrative units themselves control and that are freely accessible to everyone.
Social media are electronic platforms that are used to communicate with the public and which enable users to provide their own content for other users.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 19 June 2024, in force since 1 Aug. 2024 (AS 2024 313).

blockList.listIntroduction: Administrative units may operate profiles with interactive functions on social media, provided that on these profiles:

item.p: all persons over the age of majority resident in Switzerland can make contributions;
the administrative units can respond to users’ contributions with their own contributions; and
the administrative units can hide, delete or otherwise suppress users’ contributions.

content.p: The administrative units shall ensure that they can be contacted via their profiles.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 19 June 2024, in force since 1 Aug. 2024 (AS 2024 313).

blockList.listIntroduction: Administrative units may suppress contributions in their profiles provided:
there are specific indications that these contributions:

item.p: incite the commission of misdemeanours or felonies,
incite hatred or violence,
contain content or representations of violence that are offensive to certain persons, defamatory, threatening, discriminatory or pornographic,
encourage behaviour that seriously endangers persons’ health or safety,
contain commercial advertising, or
have been generated by a machine; or

blockList.listIntroduction: that these contributions are posted repeatedly and:

item.p: are clearly irrelevant, or
are clearly false in their content and there are specific indications that they serve the purpose of disinformation.

content.p: If an exceptionally large number of contributions are received, the suppression of contributions may be temporarily automated.
In the event of repeated or particularly serious infringements, an administrative unit may block the user for a maximum of two years.
The block shall be lifted on expiry of the blocking period if the user so requests.
Through supervision, the Federal Council, the departments and the Federal Chancellery shall ensure the fulfilment of constitutional and statutory duties.
Supervision of the Central Federal Administration is comprehensive. It shall be governed by the principles set out in Articles 11 and 12.

The subject matter, scope and principles of supervision of the decentralised Federal Administration and of the entities referred to in Article 2 paragraph 4 GAOA shall be governed by specific legislation and shall be based on the respective degree of autonomy.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 11 March 2022, in force since 1 July 2022 (AS 2022 179).

content.p: The Federal Council shall act as the owner and carry out the associated supervision and control in relation to the autonomous units in accordance with Article 8 paragraph 5 GAOA as a whole.

The department with the closest relevance to the field in question shall exercise supervision on behalf of the Federal Council, exercise the owner’s rights and serve as the contact for the management bodies of the autonomous units. In the case of autonomous units of major importance for the federal budget, it shall exercise the ownership rights jointly with the FFA. The departments to which the autonomous units are allocated and the units for which joint exercise of ownership rights with the FFA applies are listed in Annex 3.

If other departments and administrative units have a connection with the field for which an autonomous unit is responsible, they shall be consulted in relation to fulfilling the tasks in accordance with paragraph 2.

The General Secretariat of the Department shall be responsible for fulfilling the tasks in accordance with paragraph 2. The Department may delegate responsibility in writing to a state secretariat or a federal office provided there are no conflicts of interest, in particular with regard to regulation, technical supervision, appointment and subsidisation.

The FFA shall draw up the principles for the supervision and management of the federal government’s autonomous units (public corporate governance) and shall ensure the coordination of reporting. In doing so, it shall work with the departments and administrative units concerned.

blockList.listIntroduction: Control, as an instrument of supervision, serves:

item.p: the in-depth clarification of special issues arising from current events or identified grievances;
the regular review of particular areas of expertise.

content.p: As a rule, controls are carried out by special bodies that are independent of the controlled administrative unit.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 21 Aug. 2002, in force since 1 Oct. 2002 (AS 2002 2827).

article.heading: Control by the Federal Council
article.subheading: (Art. 8 paras. 3 and 4, 25 para. 2 lett. c and d, 32 lett. e GAOA)

content.p: The Federal Council and the President of the Confederation are supported by the Federal Chancellery in the exercise of their statutory control duties. For further interdepartmental clarifications, project organisations pursuant to Article 56 GAOA or an external consultant pursuant to Article 57 GAOA may be appointed.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 21 Aug. 2002, in force since 1 Oct. 2002 (AS 2002 2827).

content.p: The administrative units shall periodically and systematically review their tasks, services, processes and organisation to determine whether they are necessary and comply with the principles of Articles 11 and 12; they shall arrange for the required adjustments and reductions to be carried out measures.
The Conference of Secretaries General shall play a coordinating role.

The FFA, in consultation with the Conference of Secretaries General, shall coordinate the review under paragraph 1 with the review under Article 5 of the Subsidies Act of 5 October 1990
SR 616.1 .

section.heading: Administrative Inquiry

content.p: An administrative inquiry is a special control procedure in accordance with Articles 25 and 26 which clarifies whether there are matters in relation to which official intervention is required in the public interest.

An administrative inquiry is not directed against specific persons. A disciplinary investigation pursuant to Article 98 of the Federal Personnel Ordinance of 3 July 2001
SR 172.220.111.3 and criminal proceedings remain reserved.
An administrative inquiry may not obstruct criminal investigations or investigations by parliamentary supervisory bodies.
If a procedural conflict is foreseeable, the ordering authority shall suspend or terminate the administrative inquiry.

The heads of the departments and the Federal Chancellor shall order administrative investigations in the administrative units under their authority. They may delegate this responsibility to the administrative units subordinate to them.
If an administrative investigation affects more than one department, including the Federal Chancellery, the Federal Council shall order the investigation.

blockList.listIntroduction: An administrative investigation shall be entrusted to persons who:

item.p: meet the necessary personal, professional and technical requirements for such a task;
are not active in the area of responsibility to be investigated; and
are not simultaneously and in the same matter entrusted with disciplinary proceedings or other personnel law proceedings.

content.p: The investigation may be delegated to persons outside the Federal Administration. Such persons shall act as agents of the ordering body.
The investigative bodies may issue directives within the scope of their mandate, but may not issue rulings.

The provisions on recusal in Article 10 of the Federal Act of 20 December 1968
SR 172.021 on Administrative Procedure (APA) apply mutatis mutandis.

blockList.listIntroduction: The ordering body shall issue a written investigation mandate. It sets out in particular:

item.p: the subject of the investigation;
the details of the appointment of the investigative body;
the powers of the investigative body;
the duty to maintain official secrecy;
the remuneration to be paid to the investigative body;
the necessary aids provided;
the involvement of auxiliary bodies;
the form in which reports are submitted;
the deadlines.

content.p: Any existing files shall be attached to the investigation mandate.

The ordering authority shall notify the administrative bodies concerned of the opening of the administrative investigation, together with the reason for and purpose of the investigation and the investigating body.
It shall issue the necessary directives on the access and inspection rights of the investigative bodies and on the duty of the employees concerned to provide information.

In order to establish the facts of the case, the investigative body shall obtain evidence by the means set out in Article 12 APA
SR 172.021 . However, there is no formal examination of witnesses in an administrative investigation.
The federal authorities and employees involved in the administrative investigation are obliged to cooperate in establishing the facts of the case.

If it becomes apparent in the course of an administrative investigation that information covered by the duty of confidentiality is required from other departments or from the Federal Chancellery, the investigative body must first obtain the consent of the head of the department or of the Federal Chancellor. In other cases, Article 14 applies.
The authorities and persons involved in the administrative investigation shall have the opportunity to inspect all files that concern them and to comment on them (Art. 26-28 APA).
They have the right to be heard (Art. 29–33 APA).
The persons involved in the administrative investigation are entitled to be represented and have legal assistance.

The investigating body shall inform the persons who are to be interviewed that they may refuse to answer the questions if by doing so they may incriminate themselves in disciplinary or criminal proceedings.
It shall inform persons outside the Federal Administration who are to be interviewed that their provision of information is voluntary.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex 2 No II 14 of the Data Protection Ordinance of 31 Aug. 2022, in force since 1 Sept. 2023 (AS 2022 568).

content.p:
Each department that is requested by the investigative body to disclose personal data must ensure and is itself responsible for ensuring that the provisions of the Data Protection Act of 25 September 2020
SR 235.1 on are complied with.
The investigative body shall deliver all investigation files and a report to the ordering body.
In the report, it shall describe the process and set out the results of the investigation and proposals for further action.
The ordering authority shall inform the authorities and persons involved in an administrative investigation of the result.
The ordering authority shall decide on the consequences of an administrative investigation.
The results of an administrative investigation may be used as a basis for initiating other proceedings, in particular proceedings under personnel law.

chapter.num:
Chapter 3a

chapter.heading: Approval of Cantonal Enactments

content.p: Cantonal acts and ordinances that must be approved by the Confederation shall be submitted to the Federal Chancellery. The Federal Chancellery may require their submission.
The enactments shall be submitted as soon as they have been adopted by the competent cantonal authority. The holding of a referendum or the expiry of a referendum period need not be awaited.
The cantons may submit enactments requiring approval to the Federal Chancellery for preliminary examination.
The Federal Chancellery shall forward enactments submitted to it to the competent department.

If an enactment does not fall within the exclusive competence of a department, the Federal Chancellery shall determine which department is responsible and shall notify the other departments that have an interest.
In non-contentious cases, the Department shall grant approval within two months of submission. It shall notify the canton and the Federal Chancellery of the approval.

If the Department comes to the conclusion that approval may not be granted because the enactment is contrary to federal law or may only be granted with reservations, it shall take an interim decision within two months of submission. It shall submit the decision to the canton with a brief statement of the reasons and set a deadline for the canton to comment.
If the Department concludes on the basis of the canton’s opinion that there is no violation of federal law, it shall grant approval within two months of receipt of the canton’s opinion.
Otherwise, the Department shall submit the item of business to the Federal Council within two months with a request for approval with reservation or for refusal of approval.

chapter.num:
Chapter 3b
Inserted by No I of the O of 5 April 2006, in force since 1 June 2006 (AS 2006 1269).
chapter.heading: Agreements by the Cantons among Themselves or with Foreign Countries

content.p: The contracting cantons or a coordination office designated by them shall notify the Federal Chancellery of agreements between the cantons or with foreign countries.

blockList.listIntroduction: Notification shall be provided:

item.p: in the case of agreements between cantons: after the adoption of the draft by the intercantonal body entrusted with its preparation or after the acceptance of the agreement by at least one contracting canton;
in the case of agreements concluded by the cantons with foreign countries: before the agreement is concluded.

content.p: The text of the agreement shall be attached to the notification.

article.heading: Preliminary examination of agreements between the cantons themselves

content.p: The cantons may submit agreements among themselves to the Federal Chancellery for preliminary examination.

The Federal Chancellery shall inform the non-participating cantons (third cantons) in the form of a notice in the Federal Gazette of an agreement brought to its attention within 14 days of receipt of the agreement.
In the notice, it shall name the contracting cantons, the title of the agreement concerned and the office where the text of the agreement may be obtained or inspected.
Paragraphs 1 and 2 apply mutatis mutandis to contracts concluded by the cantons with foreign countries through the intermediation of the Confederation.
The Federal Chancellery shall forward an agreement submitted to it to the competent department.
If an agreement does not fall within the exclusive competence of a department, the Federal Chancellery shall determine the lead department and inform the other departments that have an interest.

article.heading: Notification of the result of the examination; Objection to agreements

content.p: The Department shall inform the contracting cantons or the coordination office and the Federal Chancellery of the result of the examination of the agreement within two months of notification in the Federal Gazette in accordance with Article 27q.

If the Department establishes that the agreement is contrary to the law or the interests of the Confederation, it shall raise this objection with the contracting cantons and, if appropriate, with the coordination office, and shall invite them to submit their comments.

The Department shall immediately notify the contracting cantons, the coordination office and the Federal Chancellery as to whether or not, on the basis of the opinion, the conflict with the law or the interests of the Confederation remains.
If the conflict with the law or with the interests of the Confederation persists, the Department shall request the Federal Council to raise an objection to the agreement with the Federal Assembly.

article.heading: Federal Council organisational ordinances for the departments and the Federal Chancellery

item.p: the objectives, principles and responsibilities of the departments and the Federal Chancellery;
the objectives, tasks and responsibilities of the groups and offices;

article.heading: Rules of procedure of the departments and the Federal Chancellery

blockList.listIntroduction: The departments and the Federal Chancellery shall issue rules of procedure for themselves. In particular, the following can be regulated therein:

item.p: the basic principles of the management processes in the department or in the Federal Chancellery;
the basic organisational principles of the department and the Federal Chancellery, unless they are governed by other provisions;
the delegation of signatory powers;

content.p: For interdepartmental tasks, the competent departments or the Federal Chancellery may issue joint rules of procedure.
The rules of procedure shall be publicly accessible but shall not be published in the Official Compilation of Federal Legislation.
The Federal Council, the General Secretaries’ Conference, the departments and the Federal Chancellery shall ensure the proper functioning of the administration by issuing directives and working aids.

item.p: the preparation of Federal Council business;
